name: BLE Gateway
summary: Bridges Bluetooth sensors into Signal K
description:
Scans for Bluetooth Low Energy sensors — temperature, humidity, battery monitors — and forwards their readings to a Signal K server.

Runs on the ESP32-P4 (BLE via its ESP32-C6 co-processor, which is what two gateways here use in daily service) and on the ESP32, C3, S3 and C6.

Not the ESP32-C5: it builds and scans, then reboots after about 30 seconds. BLE plus WiFi plus the Signal K client needs ~152 KB of its ~176 KB of internal RAM, the HTTP posts start failing and the health watchdog restarts the board. Its 8 MB of PSRAM does not help — what remains is task stacks and DMA buffers, which cannot live in external RAM. A C5 is a good WiFi/Signal K board, but it is not a BLE bridge.

boards.name: ESP32-C6 development board
boards.notes: The ESP32-C6-MINI-1U has no PCB antenna: without an external one the radio sees nothing, which looks exactly like a software fault.

boards.name: Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-POE-ETH
boards.notes: Never connect USB and Ethernet at the same time: powering the board from USB and PoE together damages it.
